C0.quote: We study the voting game where agents’ preferences are endogenous
C0.note: Strategic aspects (strong equilibrium) of majority voting with private signals.

C1.quote: every 𝜀-strong Bayes Nash Equilibrium with 𝜀 converging to 0
C1.note: Main results characterise equilibria and their fidelity (probability of the informed majority decision). Corollaries on informative and sincere voting are characterisation results. AX is a weak fit and is listed only for those characterisations.

C2.1.value: votes; strategy profile (votes for A or R)
C2.1.quote: Each agent 𝑛 votes for A or R.

C2.2.quote: Each agent 𝑛 votes for A or R.
C2.2.note: Binary vote between two alternatives, with a mixed strategy mapping signals to votes. Fits none of the listed formats.

C2.3.loc: Sec. 2, Utility and Types of Agents
C2.3.quote: Each agent 𝑛 has a utility which is a function of the true world state

C2.4.quote: agents may have incentives to deviate from sincere or informative voting
C2.4.note: Votes and strategies are modelled separately from utilities and signals.

C3.1.quote: Our results give merit to strategic voting.
C3.1.note: Equilibrium analysis is strategic. Informative and sincere voting are analysed as non-strategic behaviours.

C3.2.note: The non-strategic analyses (informative and sincere voting) are defined as behaviours. The input is not described as equal to a held attitude. Voting behaviour is defined as a function of signals and utilities, so the stated-sincerity question does not arise.

C4.1.note: The input is a binary vote and the format is OTH, so the applicability condition (RANK, WEAK, APPR, DICH or PAIR) is not met.

C4.2.note: The term dichotomous preferences is not used.

C5.1.quote: Fidelity is the likelihood that the informed majority decision is reached.
C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by fidelity to the informed majority decision. Expected utility is also analysed.

C5.2.quote: which is the alternative favored by the majority of the agents
C5.2.note: Evaluated against agents' preferences given the true state, which are defined separately from votes.

VOT.quote_behav: two most common non-strategic voting schemes – informative voting and sincere voting
VOT.quote_info: The signal distributions ((𝑃ℎ𝐻 , 𝑃𝑙𝐻 ), (𝑃ℎ𝐿 , 𝑃𝑙𝐿 )) are also common knowledge.
VOT.note: Voters are strategic in the equilibrium analysis and non-strategic in the informative and sincere analyses. They know the prior, the signal distributions and the type fractions, plus their own signal.

CAN.note: Alternatives are only options to be chosen.

C8.1.quote: we use the solution concept of 𝜀-strong Bayes Nash Equilibrium
C8.1.note: The strong Bayes Nash equilibrium is coalitional and Bayesian.

C8.2.quote: we use the solution concept of 𝜀-strong Bayes Nash Equilibrium

claims.quote: Our results give merit to strategic voting for making good decisions.
strategic behavior “prevails” over non-strategic behaviors in binary voting!
the goal is to make a “good” decision that reflects the real preferences

C9.2.quote: A is more preferred in 𝐻 , and R is more preferred in 𝐿.
C9.2.note: The claims rest on the signal structure, the utilities, common knowledge and strategic voting by contingent agents, and the paper states all of these. The claim that the informed majority decision is a good decision is the paper's own normative definition.

C10.1.note: The paper does not say it studies the rule only as a function of submitted inputs.
